components.name: Workspace contextual actions
components.description: Static open-menu sample with icons omitted. The 52px titlebar carries project context. The chat pane's own 40px header groups Run, files/code (folder), then the project menu at its upper right, using 28px icons aligned with the neighboring tab strip. Project check/export/delete live in this chat-scoped menu. The code pane has a 40px scrolling closable-tab strip with search/format/tree/file-menu/expand/close controls, then a path row with a 30px minimum and a 136px-wide shared 28px language selector. File-menu actions include create, protected rename/delete and close-all. Live native auto popovers retain keyboard navigation and composition guards. Both panes remain mounted; switching/closing tabs flushes edits and per-file cursor/scroll positions restore without a full-history claim.

components.name: Installed application action dialog
components.description: Static modal-content sample; existing Phosphor artwork and close icon are omitted. Live identity pairs a 48px icon with the scoped title and optional non-repeated app ID. Device and simulator sections hold their own availability and feedback. Shared 32px actions align right with 76px minimum width; read retry uses 28px. Target/source controls appear only for matching local source; one source is text, multiple sources use a shared in-app Select, preferring the installed version then latest update. Missing profiles expose an inline name/model creation form even without matching local source. Creating saves an independent profile and selects it without leaving the dialog; saving blocks duplicate submission/dismissal, failures retain the form for retry, and missing source still disables Run. Deletion opens confirmation. Identity receives initial focus; action focus, Escape/backdrop drag guard, busy protection and opener restoration retain shared Dialog behavior. This extends the pinned native/magpie system; synthetic checks do not establish physical-device execution.

components.name: Device identity card
components.description: Static offline sample of the device-detail identity card; the models-player tile content is omitted and glyphs are simplified inline SVG. Grid: 112px model column and flexible text column, 20px gap; areas model/head, model/strip, empty/details. Offline dims the model (grayscale, 0.5 opacity, 220ms ease-out, none under reduced motion). Removal is a 28px red ghost action whose accessible name equals its visible text and opens confirmation. Connectivity glyphs show on/off state only. The disclosure sets aria-expanded (aria-controls only while open) and reveals address, firmware and the unchanged DeviceKeyEditor. Container queries: 64px tile, full-width strip and icon-only actions at <=600px; stacked detail labels at <=360px; 52px tile at <=300px. Local inside the magpie shell and the user's Apple Home device direction.

narrative.overview:
This record describes the currently implemented React interface inside the GizMoth desktop application. It captures the shared titlebar and collapsible primary sidebar, project discovery and nested primary-sidebar navigation, device controls and installed-application library, Lua editor/pi-agent views, independent simulator windows, provider forms, and dialogs. Planned serial flashing and direct firmware development do not yet have an implemented visual system in the sampled sources.

The interface follows the user's compact magpie reference with system typography, neutral surfaces, compact actions, and Phosphor interface icons. Device detail follows their explicit local iPhone/Apple Home direction: compact square controls expand into dark panels with an emissive screen, a faceted glowing lamp, or an upward sound cone; outside clicks dismiss them. Application icons first open a metadata/action dialog with device run, matching-local-project simulation, and confirmed deletion. The simulator is an independent device window following the pinned magpie/Apple Simulator direction, with a flexible model stage, compact chrome and on-demand firmware/help popovers. Application snapshots are temporary requests without a persistent project association. A white identity card pairs a model tile, dimmed while offline, with the name, connection line and an on/off readings strip; Device information expands the address, firmware and device key below the strip, while red removal stays at the upper right even on narrow screens. Projects uses nested Lua/Giz/native-firmware category navigation; project contents stay inside the workspace. This remains an implementation record, not a claim of a new global visual identity. Shared Button, IconButton, Input, Select and SearchInput primitives centralize 28/32/40px size roles, padding, caret placement and interaction states.
keyCharacteristics: Shared titlebar, collapsible desktop sidebar, and independently scrolling work areas.
Compact controls, rounded containers, and thin neutral borders.
Recognizable application icons and semantic status alongside a neutral editor and shell.

rules.name: The On-Demand Configuration Rule
rules.body: Simulator firmware settings and keyboard help use native auto popovers, dismissed by outside click, Escape or their close action, without a modal veil. Keep the device stage visible around them.

rules.name: The Visible Runtime State Rule
rules.body: Keep runtime state in the footer and communicate unsupported execution through the Only Preview action, help/settings explanations and disabled install action. Availability follows actual Web Crypto, cross-origin isolation and SharedArrayBuffer capabilities in both native windows and browsers. Preserve explicit model and compatible-firmware selection, installation and start; observed packaged macOS firmware start does not establish full gameplay.

rules.name: The Explicit Formatting Rule
rules.body: The code toolbar's Format icon and Shift+Alt+F explicitly format and save the active source file. The path bar offers automatic language detection from the extension and a per-file override for Lua, JSON, JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, Markdown, YAML or plain text. Selection changes highlighting and formatter choice without renaming files; overrides last within the open workspace and are not persisted preferences. Plain text disables formatting. Formatting uses two-space indentation and a 100-column target. Lua uses StyLua 2.6 with Lua 5.4 syntax and output AST verification through native Rust or browser-demo WASM; other source languages use Prettier standalone and bundled plugins. Formatting is text-only with a 2 MiB limit and no project-owned plugin execution. Syntax failures preserve source and surface an error. The existing 500 ms autosave does not format. This record does not claim verified undo behavior.

rules.name: The Changeable-Only Footer Rule
rules.body: Only controls the user can change sit under the input. The footer holds the model trigger and, only once the provider has reported usage, a context-usage ring. Fixed facts such as the provider name, and per-project settings such as assistant permissions, belong in the project information panel, never in the footer.
